seo.description: The Long Way Round: essays on slow travel by Hana Mori. Trains, ferries, walking, and why the detour is the trip.

items.title: Thirty-one hours to Istanbul, and I would do it again
items.text: Four trains, one ferry and a border guard who wanted to talk about football. What the slow route costs, and what it gives back.
items.alt: Mountains above a lake, seen from a train window

items.title: The case for the night ferry
items.text: A cabin, a bar, the sea. Cheaper than a hotel.

items.title: How to pack for three weeks in one small bag
items.text: A list, and the four things I stopped bringing.

items.title: Lisbon on foot, hill by hill
items.text: A walk that takes a day and avoids every tram queue.

items.title: What a missed connection taught me
items.text: Six hours in a town I had never heard of.

props.title: A letter every other Sunday
props.text: The new essay, one route worth taking and nothing to buy. 3,100 readers so far.

props.title: Who writes this
props.text: Hana Mori has not taken a flight since 2019. She writes from trains, mostly, and pays for every ticket herself.
